## What was actually missing

The spec's exemption clause has four parts; only the first two were tested. `tests/test_limiter.py` now pins all four:

- `test_exempt_tenant_is_never_limited` — 200 + exact header dict across `standard` and `gold` tiers and multiple routes (300 requests each).
- `test_exempt_tenant_uses_no_bucket` — "use no bucket": the registry stays empty after exempt traffic.
- `test_exempt_requests_are_never_logged` — no `limiter.reject` WARNING for exempt traffic.

The white-box assertion on `middleware._BUCKETS` is deliberate: "uses no bucket" has no other observable effect, so nothing else can guard it.

## Verification

`python3 -m pytest -q` → **21 passed** (was 19: +2 new, 1 extended). `limiter/__init__.py` and `vendor/` untouched.

If you had a different clause in mind, say which — but note every other spec requirement already has both code and a test, so exemptions is the only candidate the plan skips.
